mainEntity.name: How long do posterior crowns typically last before needing replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Posterior crowns commonly last 10-15 years with proper care, though many function successfully for much longer periods. Longevity depends on factors including crown material, underlying tooth health, bite forces, and maintenance practices. Regular dental check-ups help monitor crown condition and identify any developing issues early, potentially extending crown lifespan through timely interventions.

mainEntity.name: Can I eat normally with a posterior crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients can eat normally with posterior crowns once they've adapted to the restoration. However, avoiding extremely hard foods, ice, and sticky sweets helps prevent crown damage. Chewing carefully and avoiding using crowned teeth for non-food items protects both the crown and underlying tooth structure. Your dentist may provide specific dietary recommendations based on your crown material and individual circumstances.

mainEntity.name: What causes pain under a dental crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pain under a crown may result from various factors including bite interference, decay beneath the crown, nerve irritation, or loose crown fit. Temperature sensitivity might indicate marginal leakage, whilst pain during biting could suggest bite problems or underlying structural issues. Persistent discomfort warrants professional evaluation to determine the cause and appropriate treatment approach.

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if my crown is failing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Signs of crown failure include persistent pain, sensitivity, visible gaps at crown margins, changes in bite feel, or crown mobility. Dark lines around crown edges might indicate decay, whilst unusual tastes could suggest bacterial penetration. Any concerning symptoms should be evaluated promptly, as early intervention often allows for simpler treatment approaches than waiting until problems become severe.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal for crowned teeth to be sensitive?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some initial sensitivity following crown placement is normal and typically resolves within a few weeks as tissues adapt. However, persistent or increasing sensitivity may indicate problems such as high bite contacts, marginal leakage, or nerve irritation. Sensitivity that develops months or years after crown placement often suggests developing complications requiring professional assessment.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the tooth under my crown fractures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treatment options for fractured teeth under crowns depend on the fracture location and severity. Minor fractures might be managed by replacing the crown, whilst extensive fractures may require additional procedures such as root canal treatment or, in severe cases, tooth extraction. Early detection through regular dental visits often allows for more conservative treatment approaches than waiting until symptoms develop.
